cohort: The study included 38,496 Chinese women without preeclampsia and 1130 Chinese women with preeclampsia, whose pregnancies occurred between January 2018 and December 2019.
finding: The study found that several maternal and pregnancy-related factors were associated with preeclampsia, which in turn significantly increased the risk of adverse maternal and neonatal perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Preeclampsia in singleton pregnancies was associated with an increased risk of cesarean section.
